general_information.Description: The course explores and focuses around the managerial functions of management, including planning, organizing, leading and controlling. The course is designed to provide basic knowledge and skills required in management and give students a comprehensive insight into human relations componnents that characterise any managerial roles, regardless of industry or functions. Various aspects of management theories will be examined and linked to current management practice in the world and Vietnam. Learning in the class will be facilitated through the use of interactive tools such as group exercise, case study discussion, role-play/activities, and projects.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Define management, its functions including planning, decision-making, and strategy development processes, and influence of organizational environments.
Describe the basic elements of organization design, encompassing forms, key situational influences, and components involved in designing effective operations systems.
Discuss human resource management practices, including recruitment, development, motivation, and leadership strategies, within the context of environmental factors.
Identify different types of organizational control mechanisms and analyze their characteristics to determine effectiveness in achieving organizational objectives.
Apply the knowledge and understanding gained from the course to evaluate real-life management situations/dilemma and practices in both local and global business contexts.
Develop leadership and management potential through the integration of theoretical knowledge with practical skills and self-awareness.
Understand the ethical and social responsibility issues in real-life management situations.

You own a chain of ten shoe-cleaning shops in Ho Chi Minh City. You are concerned about the customer service problems that have been reported in a few stores. However, the employees always provide outstanding customer service with positive attitudes whenever you visit a store, whether for the entire day or just a few hours. During your visit, you observed that the clerks carefully removed dirt from shoes, washed shoelaces by hand, and cleaned difficult materials such as canvas or suede shoes exceptionally well. Nonetheless, during these unscheduled visits, some customers complained about problems with their previous orders; such as improper dirt removal. Some customers even brought their shoes to the store to be redone. In addition, customers also send private messages and even comment on the company fan page that the wait time for services is too long. You and the other store managers are meeting today to address this problem. Identify and describe the major content perspective on motivation in this case. Then, choose one theory and describe the actions that you might take to increase employees' motivation.
